pages.text: Jennie Finch Empowerment Award opens opportunities beyond softball Skip to Content VERO BEACH, Fla. -- Kourtney Jones-Caldwell and Alina Elias have each had their moment with Jennie Finch. Jones-Caldwell received the Jennie Finch Empowerment Award last year, while Elias was recognized with the award during this year’s All-Star Week. pages.text: Jeremy Deller (born 1966) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Jeremy Deller (b. 1966, London) is a British artist, known for his work with video, installation and performances. He produced The Triumph of Art , a nationwide performance that closed the National Gallery’s Bicentenary celebrations in 2025, in partnership with galleries, theatre groups and art schools across the UK. He celebrated the role of art in civic life, as a driver for festivity and community. He created the Manod Slate Tablet as part of this project to commemorate the time when the nation’s paintings were sent to Manod Quarry in North Wales for safe keeping during the Second World War. Deller studied History of Art at the Courtauld Institute and at Sussex University. He began making artworks in the early 1990s, often showing them outside conventional galleries. In 1993, while his parents were on holiday, he secretly used the family home for an exhibition titled Open Bedroom . Four years later, he produced the musical performance Acid Brass with the Williams-Fairey Band and began making art in collaboration with other people. In 2000, with fellow artist Alan Kane, Deller began a collection of items that illustrate the passions and pastimes of people from across Britain and the social classes. Treading a fine line between art and anthropology, Folk Archive is a collection of objects which touch on diverse subjects such as Morris Dancing, gurning competitions and political demonstrations. Espresso. Chestnut. Cacao. Ganache. Coffee bean. Truffle. Mocha. Caramel. Hazelnut. Nobody seems terribly keen to call it brown. Brown has never been the sexiest word in the paintbox. Red is passion. Black is chic. Pink is romance. Blue is serenity. Brown is the colour of wheelie bins. Except that right now, brown – specifically the deep, glossy, edible-looking chocolate end of the spectrum – is probably the chicest colour you can wear. It is probably not incidental that we so often describe it in terms of what we eat or drink. In this role, she provides executive leadership for the Federal Aviation Administration's efforts to safely integrate advanced aviation technologies into the National Airspace System (NAS), including uncrewed aircraft systems (UAS), electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, counter-UAS technologies, and other emerging entrants. She is responsible for developing enterprise-wide strategic and business plans, overseeing research and integration initiatives, coordinating with the Department of Transportation, other federal agencies, industry, and international stakeholders, and advancing policies that enable the safe expansion of advanced aviation technologies. Ms. Jones has more than 15 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in the Federal Aviation Administration, specializing in executive operations, strategic planning, national security, program management, and organizational governance. Jessica Kunkle Jessica Kunkle Jessica Kunkle is NNSA’s Associate Administrator for the Office of Infrastructure. She brings over 15 years of diverse experience, spanning infrastructure, nonproliferation, procurement, and budgeting. In her current role, Ms. Kunkle is charged with modernizing the Nuclear Security Enterprise to support the agency’s vital national security missions. Her passion for innovation, agility, and delivering results have enabled her to push the boundaries of NNSA’s real property acquisition strategy and accelerate infrastructure modernization via bold, proactive streamlining and non-traditional delivery approaches. During her NNSA tenure, Ms. Kunkle has held diverse leadership roles, including Manager of the Environmental Management Los Alamos Field Office, Deputy Associate Administrator for Infrastructure Lifecycle Management, and Acting Manager of NNSA’s Savannah River Field Office. She also led agency-wide improvement initiatives in the NNSA Program Executive Office and helped to secure vulnerable nuclear materials and radiological facilities around the world in the Office of Global Threat Reduction. pages.text: Jesus de Miguel death: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono experiencing 'most difficult days of my life' - BBC Sport Figure caption, Fans pay respects to Tenerife's De Miguel By David Watkinson , BBC Sport senior journalist and Ffion Wynne , BBC Sport journalist Published 4 November 2026 FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday. The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week. Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally". "These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement. "I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened. "I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. "I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing. "Rest in peace, Jesus." The Canary island is in mourning for the Tenerife striker, who died from injuries sustained in a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a match on Monday. The 30-year-old had quickly established himself as a club favourite, scoring 11 goals in his first season as Tenerife were promoted to the second tier of Spanish football. But now the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium has become a shrine to the player, with hundreds of people gathering throughout the past few days to lay flowers, light candles and pay their respects. Bouquets, rosettes sent by clubs from across Spain, prayer cards, photographs, children's drawings and scarves have been laid around the grounds outside gate nine. It is a deeply moving scene. Fans and residents stand in silence, taking in the tributes. Many are visibly tearful as the scale of the loss begins to sink in at the very place the incident happened. pages.text: Jesus de Miguel: Funeral of Tenerife forward takes place as family thankful for support - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in the town of Navahermosa in Spain on Thursday By Ben Collins BBC Sport journalist Published 5 November 2026 Jesus de Miguel's family said "the mark he has left on so many people" was something they would always remember as the footballer's funeral took place on Thursday. The Tenerife forward, who was 30, died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second division match on Monday. After colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono, De Miguel lay motionless on the pitch while being treated by medical staff and was taken to hospital, where he died at 07:00 GMT on Tuesday. Owono was sent off for the challenge and the game was abandoned. De Miguel's funeral was held in his parents' hometown of Navahermosa, Toledo, about 125km from the Spanish capital Madrid. His Tenerife team-mates carried his coffin before the service at San Miguel Arcangel. Current Spain coach Luis de la Fuente was among the mourners, along with Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, Atletico Madrid chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin and former Real and Spain coach Jose Antonio Camacho. De Miguel's agent, Manuel Hernandez, issued a statement on behalf of the family, which read: "Thank you for loving him, for remembering him and for being with us. pages.text: Jesus de Miguel: Jesus Owono left out of Equatorial Guinea squad after death of Tenerife player - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Jesus Owono helped Equatorial Guinea to the quarter-finals of the 2021 Afcon but the National Thunder suffered a group-stage exit at the 2025 finals in Morocco Published 5 November 2026 Goalkeeper Jesus Owono will miss Equatorial Guinea's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers this month following the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday. Owono said he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" in a statement issued by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, adding that it is "very hard to come to terms with what has happened". Equatorial Guinea's football federation (Feguifut) said that the 25-year-old had requested to be left out of coach Vincenzo Alberto Annese's squad. Feguifut president Venancio Tomas Micha had previously said his organisation was offering "all our human and professional backing" to the player. Owono has been first-choice keeper for the National Thunder since November 2020 and has featured at the past three Afcons. Equatorial Guinea face Zimbabwe in a double-header in Group E, with a home match in Bata on Thursday, 12 November before a trip to Harare four days later. The two teams sit level on three points after two rounds of matches, with DR Congo top of the standings on six points and Sierra Leone pointless at the bottom of the table. Close jfd553's Diary Mapping Icefields Parkway, Part 1: A two-year mapping journey Posted by jfd553 on 4 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 6 November 2026. I spent two years mapping the areas surrounding one of the most beautiful drives in the world. Each morning, I looked forward to discovering and mapping an area adjacent to a one I did the day before. This diary entry serves as an introduction to a series of texts covering the challenges I encountered and how I overcame them. Included below are a few snapshots taken in the field, which capture the majestic landscapes along the Icefields Parkway. I have also added a “before and after” map excerpt, as well as a short video, to illustrate how my work gradually took shape over time. The Place The Icefields Parkway (Highway 93N), in Alberta, owes its name to the spectacular icefields and glaciers that line the road. The parkway, which is a 232 km stretch of highway cutting through Banff and Jasper National Parks, attracts between 1.2 million and 2 million visitors per year. The parkway offers exceptional alpine landscape, with glaciers, rivers, turquoise lakes, and breathtaking mountain views directly from the roadside (Figure 1). Best of all, many of these landmarks can be reached in a single day’s hike (Figure 2). Figure 1: North Saskatchewan River alongside the parkway. pages.text: JJ Gabriel transfer news: Real Madrid confident of signing Manchester United forward - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, JJ Gabriel joined Manchester United in 2022 By Simon Stone Manchester United reporter Published 4 November 2026 Real Madrid are confident of winning the race to sign Manchester United forward JJ Gabriel after reaching a verbal agreement with the teenager. The 16-year-old is registered at United, but has not been back to the club since walking out in September. Gabriel, who played against Atletico Madrid on United's pre-season tour, had been expected to become the club's youngest debutant in September's Carabao Cup tie against Brighton. However, he has opted to look elsewhere for senior football and has been training on his own in Spain. His availability alerted clubs around Europe, including Barcelona and Paris St-Germain, but Real now expect to sign the youngster in January. Though no club-to-club talks have been held, sources have told BBC Sport Real have verbally agreed a deal with Gabriel and his representatives. Gabriel, who scored a hat-trick on his Uefa Youth League debut, has secured a European Union passport, which is expected to make it easier for him to sign for a club outside England. United would be due compensation should Gabriel leave, although the figure will be lower if he signs for a club outside the Premier League. Job Corps is the largest nationwide residential career training program in the country and has been operating for more than 50 years. The program helps eligible young people ages 16 through 24 complete their high school education, trains them for meaningful careers, and assists them with obtaining employment. Job Corps has trained and educated over two million individuals since 1964. At Job Corps, students have access to room and board while they learn skills in specific training areas for up to three years. In addition to helping students complete their education, obtain career technical skills and gain employment, Job Corps also provides transitional support services, such as help finding employment, housing, child care, and transportation. Job Corps graduates either enter the workforce or an apprenticeship, go on to higher education, or join the military. Considering Job Corps? Learn More Today! Key Benefits Job Corps offers career technical skills training in 10 high-growth industry sectors: Advanced Manufacturing Automotive and Machine Repair Construction Finance and Business Healthcare Homeland Security Hospitality Information Technology Renewable Resources and Energy Transportation Students can earn a high school diploma or the equivalent, and college credits. pages.text: John Gibson (1790 - 1866) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content John Gibson (1790–1866) was a Welsh sculptor, central to the Neoclassical movement. In 1817, he moved to Rome, where he was apprenticed to Antonio Canova (1757–1822), Italy’s leading sculptor, and was later viewed as his natural successor. Feeling the absence of a British art school in Rome, in 1821 Gibson joined other artists including sculptors Richard Westmacott the Younger (1799–1872) and Lawrence Macdonald (1799–1878), and painters Joseph Severn (1793–1879) and Charles Eastlake (1793–1865) – later the first Director of the National Gallery – to establish the British Academy of Arts in Rome. He spent the rest of his life in the city, returning to England only occasionally for work. In 1829, Gibson was elected to the Academy of Saint Luke, Rome, and by 1831, became a resident academician. He was made an associate of the Royal Academy in London in 1833 and became a full Academician in 1836. His studio in Rome was a hub of activity, producing not only idealised statues from Classical mythology in marble, on which his reputation was founded, but also bas-reliefs and portrait busts of contemporary subjects and replicas of his popular works. His designs became well known through being reproduced as jewellery and cameos. Enjoying prestigious royal patronage in later years, he created several works for Queen Victoria (1819–1901). She is considered England’s first female art historian. Born in Dublin and educated in London, she began her career as a governess before rising to prominence with her literary work. Over her thirty-year career, necessitated through having to support several family members, she published a range of influential books. In Memoirs of Celebrated Female Sovereigns (1831) and Characteristics of Women, Moral, Poetical and Historical (1832), she strongly advocated women’s roles in history and literature. Through publications such as Sacred and Legendary Art (1848–64), she later established herself as a leading art critic. Other works, including Handbook to the Public Galleries (1842) and Memoirs of the Early Italian Painters (1845), played a crucial role in educating the public about art and supporting the National Gallery’s mission to reach broad audiences. Her works are often informed by her deep knowledge of the art and culture of Italy and Germany. It was painted at the height of John Singer Sargent’s fame as a society portraitist and was widely praised when it was exhibited at the New Gallery, London in 1900. Victoria is shown aged six or seven and the setting can be identified as Sargent’s studio from the luxurious Aubusson carpet which features in many of his portraits. The grand but simple composition follows the conventions of adult portraiture but moderated for a child subject. She stands confidently and directly meets the viewer’s gaze. Although she is not dressed for horse riding, her costume references the country pursuit of hunting through her striking red coat and the hunting crop held in her hands. Her outfit is completed by a crisp white dress, polished black shoes and an extravagant bonnet decorated with bow and feathers. The Five Points Jam brings together more than 30 musicians for high-energy performances. Richard Mukuze By Sam Kemp Published November 18, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). The jazz saxophonist Stan Getz once said that the best music sounds “like a good conversation among friends”. Right now, some of the most interesting musical conversations in London are happening at its grassroots venues, where open jam sessions are giving musicians of all levels a platform to improvise, hone their craft and form new friendships. Participants may not know their fellow musicians, let alone the genre or dynamic, so there’s no choice but to embrace whatever the night brings. It’s about getting lost in music, together. London’s open jam scene really took hold in the years following the Covid lockdown — a period when music-lovers were looking for new ways to connect in a city beset by independent venue closures and the ongoing effects of social isolation. New Zealand's Southern Alps are home to one of the world's rarest birds: the black stilt. Natasha Bazika By Natasha Bazika Published June 11, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). Clouds move quickly across the Mackenzie Basin, dragging shadows over braided riverbeds and dry tussock plains that stretch towards New Zealand’s Southern Alps. One moment, the landscape is washed silver; the next, it disappears beneath a sweep of weather rolling over the mountains. I’m heading deeper into this high country on a window of borrowed time, crossing the 46,950-acre wilderness of Glenmore Station, a merino sheep, deer and cattle station. Hours earlier, the same storm front had grounded my helicopter flight to the country’s highest whisky bar — The Bad Decision, on a saddle above Glenmore Station — before it could leave the tarmac. Now, I’m racing a temporary clearing in the weather to find something far more elusive than a dram of mountain liquor: the black stilt, or kakī in Māori, one of the rarest birds on the planet. “The Mackenzie Basin has its own weather system,” says guide Ben Laffan, who’s taking me on Tekapo Adventures’ Black Stilt birding tour , a newly launched birdwatching experience, directing our four-wheel drive up a rough track. The 41-year-old Venezuelan posted a message on social media on Sunday about being held by America's Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency. "I can confirm that my friend Jorge Linares, former WBA world champion, is in ICE custody," said WBA president Gilberto Mendoza , external on social media. pages.description: People know Josh Kerr the athlete. But are there two Josh Kerrs? The mile world record holder talks about disguising alcohol-free cider, entering races under a false name and his granny keeping him humble.
pages.text: Josh Kerr: The Making of the Man Behind the Shades - BBC Sport By Richard Winton BBC Sport Scotland You know Josh Kerr, right? The guy with the shades. The fastest man to ever run a mile. Scottish, but with a curious transatlantic accent. Slicked-back hair. Beard. Usually got a medal of some kind slung around his neck. No stranger to telling you what he thinks. That's Kerr the competitor, one of the foremost faces in world athletics, and a man who rampaged around London's Olympic Stadium in three minutes 42.66 seconds in July to set a new world record - then followed it up with a home Commonwealth gold and an imperious triumph at the Ultimate Championship. Kerr recognises the description, smiling as it's articulated. But is there another version of him? Speaking to him during one of his regular returns to Scotland from his New Mexico base, it becomes clear there is. There's scant chat about records, medals and his enjoyably niggly rivalry with Jakob Ingebrigtsen. Instead, he talks about disguising alcohol-free cider, entering races under a false name, cold-calling universities, being starstruck meeting Scotland's rugby players and his granny keeping him humble. This is the Kerr who spent the thick end of an hour on a chilly August evening taking selfies, signing his name and sharing his wisdom with young fans at Scotstoun after his Commonwealth medal presentation. The Kerr who is still a regular visitor to first club Edinburgh AC's training sessions. This is Uncle Josh, who is heading for a party with his nephews after this chat. pages.text: Josh Naylor, Mariners have five-year free-agent contract Skip to Content SEATTLE -- Josh Naylor made it clear how much he enjoyed his three-month stint with the Mariners this past season, while Seattle’s front office made it very publicly clear at the offseason’s outset that a reunion with the slugging first baseman was its No. 1 priority . Turns out, getting a deal done was maybe as simple as that. Naylor and the Mariners finalized a five-year free-agent contract on Monday, the club announced, after he completed a physical in Seattle. The deal is worth $92.5 million, sources told MLB.com on Monday afternoon, but the club did not confirm the value. It also includes a full no-trade clause. As expected, it is the richest free-agent contract for a position player in Seattle since Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto took over after the 2015 season. The previous high was a two-year, $24 million deal given to Mitch Garver in the 2023-24 offseason. The most lucrative deal in franchise history was Robinson Cano's 10-year, $240 million contract during the 2013-14 offseason. Naylor and the Mariners will hold a press conference on Tuesday morning. “Ensuring that Josh remains a Mariner for the long haul was a priority for us,” Dipoto said in a statement. “Josh’s intelligence, intensity, toughness, and competitiveness show up every day. Carter serves as Associate Administrator in SBA’s Office of Investment and Innovation, where he oversees the administration of the Small Business Investment Company (SBIC) and the Small Business Investment Research/Small Business Technology Transfer Research (SBIR/STTR) programs. Prior to SBA, Mr. Carter co-founded and served as Co-Chief Investment Officer at Sepio Capital, a multi-family office and institutional investment firm based in Salt Lake City, Utah. Before then, Mr. Carter was a senior portfolio manager and institutional consultant at Bank of America Merrill Lynch. Mr. Carter also held several roles at Goldman Sachs, including proprietary trader, senior equity research analyst, and financial analyst. Mr. Carter holds a degree in Social Studies cum laude from Harvard University, and an MBA from The Wharton School. He is also a Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) and CAIA Charterholder.
